# Week 6 Rescue the supply cube

> [Download the Word version](W06_rescue_Speaker_Notes.docx) · This Markdown copy is generated from the DOCX. Update the DOCX, then run `python scripts/sync_documents.py --write` from the repository root. Print layout, page breaks, headers/footers, and writing-space height remain in Word.

Speaker notes for the one-hour rescue exercise using the printed Week 6 field.

### Class setup

**Goal**  Teams use a passive plow to move a supply cube, then test one guide change. They can explain what deliver() does and check the cube result independently of the sensor result.

**Print**  Print W06\_Class\_Print\_Packet.pdf once on US Letter, Actual Size (100%), single-sided, with automatic page orientation. Page 1 is the checklist and page 2 is the assembly guide. Kit A uses pages 3–7 and Kit B uses pages 8–12. Pages 13–17 are team sheets, 18–21 are build cards, and page 22 is attendance.

**Assemble**  For each 24 × 60 cm lane, trim and join A–B–C, match the paired ticks and tape from behind. Set the strip’s near edge at 25 cm on B. Cut the paired cube-start, bay-near and bay-far tabs. Place tabs along the outside edges with arrows facing across the lane, keeping the sensor path clear.

**Rehearse both kits**  Center downward sensor D at START facing C. Open W06\_rescue.py (motor A left, B right, SPEED = 200). Attach the mentor plow while stopped. Check wheel and floor clearance and an unobstructed sensor view. Recheck each kit’s Week 5 threshold over white, seams and dark. With strip and cube removed, run through L and confirm the whole robot has clear runout. Restore the strip, rehearse with the cube, and mark the bay using a controlled M trial.

**Stations**  Two robot stations and two build tables serve T1–T4. Bring six lightweight cubes, two mentor plows, four team build packs, four mounting proxies, tape and rulers. Open the slides with Presenter View notes and save separate team projects.

## Slide 1 Rescue the supply cube

**Timing**  0–5 minutes

**Open**  Hold up the cube and show the passive plow. Today the robot moves a supply cube and stops at the same kind of dark strip the teams tested in Week 5. The mission succeeds when M appears over the strip and the whole cube base reaches its marked bay.

**Ask**  What did the sensor measure in Week 5? How will we tell whether the cube came with the robot? Listen for reflection and a separate check of the cube.

## Slide 2 Mark the cube start and rescue bay

**Timing**  5–10 minutes

**Show the start**  Use the assembled lane. Center sensor D between the START marks on tile A, with the robot facing C. Set the near edge of the dark strip on B at the 25 cm marks. With the robot stopped, center the cube just ahead of the plow. Place one CUBE START tab at each side, both arrows lined up across the cube center. Point to the matching marks in the left drawing.

**Show the bay**  Use the rehearsed mentor run or demonstrate it now. Confirm M and that the cube stayed in front. Place a left and right BAY NEAR tab just before the resting cube and a left and right BAY FAR tab just beyond it. The entire cube base should fit between those edges and within the lane. Point to the right drawing.

**Fix the marks**  The drawings show the order of parts. The bay depends on the actual plow and where the cube rests. Keep the marked cube start, robot start, strip and bay fixed for the team comparison.

## Slide 3 How deliver stops the robot

**Timing**  10–14 minutes

**Trace**  The complete W06\_rescue.py recipe calls await deliver(). The function shows R and calls seek\_marker(threshold) using each kit’s rechecked Week 5 number. The helper checks reflected light before each short move and again after the last move. It reports a marker when the reading is below the threshold.

**Ask**  If M appears and the cube has fallen to the side, did the sensor stop succeed? Did the delivery succeed? Listen for yes to the first if the sensor is on the strip, and no to the second. L means the movement limit was reached.

**Predict**  Ask which single guide change might keep the cube lined up. Keep the sensor threshold fixed during the design comparison unless a mentor must recalibrate.

## Slide 4 Build a plow and test the baseline

**Timing**  14–26 and 26–38 minutes

**Rotate**  T1/T3 start at the robots while T2/T4 build, then switch. At the robots use driver, navigator and observer. At the build table use builder, parts manager and tester. Rotate jobs every four minutes.

**Robot station**  Use the mentor plow for the baseline. The navigator resets sensor D at START and the cube at the paired cube-start tabs. The driver runs the project. The observer records M or L and whether the full cube base is inside the bay.

**Build station**  Make a low flat bumper with a removable mount. Try a short side guide or one change to guide width. Hand-push on the proxy. A mentor approves the mount and checks floor, wheel and sensor clearance with the robot stopped.

## Slide 5 Change one part and retest

**Timing**  38–44 minutes T1/T3, then 44–50 minutes T2/T4

**Test**  Install the approved team plow. Reset the same cube and robot at their marked starts. Keep the 25 cm strip, threshold and rescue bay fixed. Compare the chosen guide feature with the baseline. Rotate jobs every two minutes.

**Diagnose**  If the cube veers or slips, check guide width and cube placement. If the robot stalls, check for dragging parts. If the sensor misses, hold the robot still and check the sensor view and the reading on the same surfaces. Fix one issue and try again.

**Record**  Write one design change, the sensor result and the cube result. A useful trial gives evidence even if only one part worked.

## Slide 6 Explain what happened to the cube

**Timing**  50–54 minutes reflection and 54–60 minutes pack

**Ask**  Give each child a brief turn. What did deliver() ask the robot to do? What did the sensor detect? Which part of the plow helped the cube stay on course? Accept an observation, a quick demonstration or one sentence.

**Close**  Save the team’s tested project and note both results. Stop both hubs and store the marked fields, cubes and labeled builds for reuse. Follow YMCA pickup procedures.
